open_points.subject: A03 outcome precedence
open_points.text:
any recorded hit makes the execution `sandbox_violation` under the order of rule 5, even when the code catches it and returns a conforming output: `timeout` and `resource_exhausted` still come first.

Outcomes are closed and checked in this order, the first that holds deciding: wall deadline passed — `timeout`; a limit hit (memory, process count, scratch, `output_bytes`) — `resource_exhausted`; a trap of rule 4 raised — `sandbox_violation`; the module failed to load, has no `run`, raised, or the process exited abnormally — `crashed`; the returned dict does not have exactly the output ports, or a value fails its port's schema, or a file output is not `bytes` — `contract_violation`; otherwise the execution succeeded.

If that cannot be confirmed the output is discarded, the execution is recorded `crashed` with detail `cleanup_failed`, and the kernel process stops; runs it left `running` are recovered on the next start (A14 rule 5).
open_points.question: When cleanup is unconfirmed together with a timeout, resource limit, recorded trap, abnormal exit or contract violation, does cleanup override the rule 5 order and force `crashed` with `cleanup_failed`, or does the first rule 5 outcome remain?
options: Cleanup always overrides and the outcome is `crashed` with detail `cleanup_failed`.
Rule 5 keeps precedence, so timeout, resource exhaustion or a trap can remain the outcome despite unconfirmed cleanup.
Cleanup overrides only some earlier outcomes; the exact precedence table must be stated.
open_points.default_guess: Follow A03-4 and A03-5: cleanup always overrides and records `crashed` with detail `cleanup_failed`.

witness.initial: A sandbox execution has no timeout or resource exhaustion; its code calls `time.time()`, catches the trap and returns a conforming output, but afterward removal of the exchange directory cannot be confirmed.
events: The sandbox records the clock trap before raising it.
The function catches the error and returns conforming output.
The parent cannot confirm cleanup of the execution environment.
outcomes: Rule 4 together with rule 5 records `sandbox_violation` because a trap was recorded and no timeout or resource exhaustion occurred.
Rule 7 and A03-4/A03-5 record `crashed` with detail `cleanup_failed`, discard the output and stop the kernel process.
witness.observer: The requesting agent and every later reader of the TrialExecution or NodeExecution.

open_points.subject: A15 value-size precedence
open_points.text: A value a node produces — a function output or a service output — above `stored_value_bytes_max` is checked only after the execution or the response has otherwise succeeded, so A03's `resource_exhausted` for `output_bytes` wins when both hold;
open_points.question: If a function output exceeds both `output_bytes` and `stored_value_bytes_max` and cleanup is also unconfirmed, does A15 still require `resource_exhausted`, or does A03-4 require `crashed` with `cleanup_failed`?
options: `resource_exhausted` wins whenever both size bounds are exceeded, even if cleanup is unconfirmed.
A15's statement is conditional on confirmed cleanup and must say so.
open_points.default_guess: Treat A15's precedence statement as conditional on confirmed cleanup; otherwise A03-4 makes the outcome `crashed` with `cleanup_failed`.

witness.initial: A function returns a value exceeding both `output_bytes` and `stored_value_bytes_max`, and cleanup of its environment cannot be confirmed.
events: The function returns the oversized value.
The parent detects the output ceiling violation.
outcomes: A15's unqualified statement records `resource_exhausted` because the `output_bytes` failure wins when both size conditions hold.
A03-4 records `crashed` with detail `cleanup_failed` because `cleanup_unconfirmed` overrides `resource_exhausted`.
witness.observer: The caller and trace readers, who see different execution statuses and details.

open_points.subject: A03-3 Required tests
open_points.text:
1. A03-3: Code that calls `time.time()`, `os.urandom`, opens a socket or reads `/etc`
   concludes `sandbox_violation`, also when it swallows the error and returns a
   conforming output.
   [witness: verification:kernel_a03_trap_hit_is_sandbox_violation]
open_points.question: Which Required tests item must show the newly added `cleanup_unconfirmed` exclusion in A03-3 by combining a recorded trap with unconfirmed cleanup and asserting the required outcome?
options: Extend this test to include a trap plus unconfirmed cleanup and require `crashed` with `cleanup_failed`, not `sandbox_violation`.
Add a separate A03-3 Required tests item for the combined trap-and-cleanup case.
Remove `cleanup_unconfirmed` from A03-3 if trap precedence is intended instead.
open_points.default_guess: Add a separate A03-3 test in which the trap is recorded and cleanup is unconfirmed, asserting `crashed` with `cleanup_failed`.

witness.initial: Two implementations conform to all currently described A03-3 Required tests; neither existing A03-3 test combines a trap with unconfirmed cleanup.
events: Implementation one applies the new cleanup override after a recorded trap.
Implementation two applies the prose rule that any recorded trap is a sandbox violation unless timeout or resource exhaustion occurred.
The existing A03-3 Required tests are run.
outcomes: Implementation one passes the existing tests and would record `crashed(cleanup_failed)` in the combined case.
Implementation two passes the existing tests and would record `sandbox_violation` in the combined case.
witness.observer: A later test author or caller encountering the untested combined condition.

open_points.subject: A03-4 Required tests
open_points.text:
11. A03-5: When removal of the exchange directory cannot be confirmed, the execution is
    recorded `crashed` with detail `cleanup_failed`, its output is discarded and
    the kernel process stops.
    [witness: verification:kernel_a03_unconfirmed_cleanup_stops_kernel]
open_points.question: Which Required tests line naming A03-4 must demonstrate that its new `cleanup_unconfirmed` branch overrides every otherwise applicable member of `first_of(timeout, resource_exhausted, sandbox_violation, crashed, contract_violation, succeeded)`?
options: Make item 11 name A03-4 as well and cover cleanup combined with every otherwise applicable outcome.
Add a separate A03-4 precedence test covering the combined cases.
State that only an otherwise successful execution needs to test the cleanup branch, leaving interactions with other outcomes unspecified.
open_points.default_guess: Add an A03-4 precedence test covering unconfirmed cleanup together with timeout, resource exhaustion, a trap, an ordinary crash, a contract violation and an otherwise successful result.

witness.initial: Two implementations both record `crashed` with `cleanup_failed` when cleanup alone is unconfirmed and therefore both pass item 11.
events: Implementation one checks `cleanup_unconfirmed` before all ordinary outcomes.
Implementation two applies the rule 5 outcome first and applies `cleanup_failed` only when no earlier failure exists.
A trapped execution is run and its cleanup cannot be confirmed.
outcomes: Implementation two records `sandbox_violation`; both implementations still pass the existing cleanup-only Required test.
witness.observer: The caller, trace readers and the later agent binding Required tests to checks.
